links.outcome: Readability (four indices and averaged composite reading grade level) of GPT-5 Thinking responses; expert-rated accuracy
links.effect: Prompt 2 had significantly lower reading grade levels than Prompt 1 across all four indices (P < 0.001), with no significant difference in word count (P = 0.12) or sentence count (P = 0.63). Mean accuracy was comparable (4.54 ± 0.63 vs 4.52 ± 0.59, P = 0.75).
links.tradeoff: The resulting grade level remained above widely recommended patient-education thresholds. No significant loss of expert-rated accuracy was reported.
links.quote: Prompt 2 produced significantly lower readability levels than Prompt 1 across all indices (P < 0.001).

links.comparator_used: Standard prompt (Prompt 1) without patient audience specification
links.outcome: Readability of GPT-5 Thinking responses for a patient audience; expert-rated accuracy
links.effect: Patient-focused Prompt 2 gave significantly lower readability levels across all indices (P < 0.001) without significant differences in word count (P = 0.12) or sentence count (P = 0.63). Accuracy was 4.54 ± 0.63 vs 4.52 ± 0.59 (P = 0.75).
links.tradeoff: The resulting grade level remained above widely recommended patient-education thresholds.
